claims.text: The target material is pristine, defect-free, oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr with a single-phase BCC structure.
The proposed model combines first-principles/DFT calculations with a semi-empirical multiscale treatment.
The model computes full phonon dispersions rather than relying solely on a Debye temperature.
The model independently assesses electronic transport using electron-scattering parameters.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Keeping oxygen below 0.1 wt.% avoids significant extrinsic effects on thermal transport.
Intrinsic atomic-scale lattice distortions and multielement chemical complexity govern phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicit phonon-dispersion calculations and independent electron-scattering calculations decouple lattice and electronic heat transport.
Treating phonon and electron transport independently provides greater fidelity than using a single effective parameter such as Debye temperature.
For defect-free, oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr, the model can predict total thermal conductivity within ±20% of experiment.
The model will reduce predictive error by about 30% relative to conventional Debye- or DFT-elasticity-based approaches.
The claimed predictive range is approximately 200–1200 K.
Conventional approaches use Debye-temperature lattice models or combine DFT-derived elastic properties with simple electronic-transport estimates.
Conventional approaches often assume perfect, defect-free bulk crystals.
Conventional approaches intermix lattice and electronic contributions or fail to separate them explicitly.
The proposed model may not apply to HfNbTaTiZr containing about 1 wt.% oxygen or significant microstructural defects.
Phonon-electron interactions in chemically complex alloys remain only partially characterized.
A deviation greater than ±20% from measured total thermal conductivity over the stated range would falsify the accuracy claim.
Failure of separately measured lattice and electronic contributions to reconcile with the model's predictions would falsify its decoupling mechanism.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis defines an applicability range of approximately 200–1200 K, while the conditions include temperatures below 200 K and the falsification experiment begins at 150 K. It is therefore unclear whether failures from 150 K to 200 K count against the hypothesis.
The target is variously described as oxygen-free and as permitting oxygen below 0.1 wt.%; the experiment again calls for an oxygen-free sample. These are not equivalent sample specifications.
